tool.help:
**MiniMak TBR Wedge Simulation**
Runs a fixed-source OpenMC neutronics calculation on a 10° toroidal wedge of the MiniMak with reflective boundary conditions. Reflective BCs mean the result is the whole-machine TBR — no manual area scaling needed.
**Blanket stack (inboard → outboard):**
1. Plasma (14.1 MeV D-T neutron source) 2. Vacuum gap (first-wall standoff) 3. **First wall** — tungsten or SS316, typically 2–5 mm 4. **Beryllium multiplier** — optional (n,2n) layer to boost TBR; set to 0 to disable 5. **Blanket** — choice of three materials, all with parametric thickness and Li-6 enrichment: - *FLiBe* (Li₂BeF₄) — molten salt, good neutron moderation, strong Be(n,2n) contribution - *Pb-16Li* — lead-lithium eutectic, low pumping power, DEMO/HCLL standard - *Pure Li* — highest lithium density, maximum breeding potential but challenging to handle 6. Void / vessel shell
**Outputs:**
- ``TBR`` — Tritium Breeding Ratio (mean ± 1σ) - Geometry PNG — visual confirmation of the simulated cross-section
**Tips:**
- Natural Li enrichment (7.5%) at MiniMak scale gives TBR ~ 0.1–0.7 depending on thickness - Try 2–5 cm Be multiplier to see the boost effect - Enriching Li-6 to ~50% can push TBR above 1.0 even at small blanket thickness
